highlights.description: Postman collections for every AAuth (draft-11) access mode, generated by pidl from the AAuth protocol document in agent-protocols, so the requests, order and checks match the AAuth walkthrough step for step

One Docker Compose file runs the aauth-go sandbox and, as an optional second part, the Petstore as an AAuth resource, with Newman runs of both collections: 21 requests and 98 assertions for the access modes, 10 requests and 47 assertions for the Petstore
`make demo` shows a real run beside the AAuth walkthrough: every message the sandbox saw, matched to the protocol's steps, with tokens decoded and raw values masked

added.description: Signed AAuth collection: agent identity, resource-managed access (two-party), person identity, PS authorization (three-party) and federated authorization (four-party), as the sandbox's demo resources perform them, with the sandbox environment
Mock collection that carries the walkthrough's example responses, for reading the flows on a Postman mock server
Petstore collection: browsing the pets with the agent's identity, and placing an order that is challenged for a person token, then an auth token, before it goes through
PIDL documents the collections are generated from: `pidl/aauth_sandbox.json` and `pidl/aauth_petstore.json`, each extending the AAuth document from agent-protocols
Signed requests tell the sandbox's signing helper how to sign with the `Signature-Key` header: a saved token by its `typ`, the helper's own agent token, enrollment or a header web key
`make demo`, `make demo-omniagent` and `make demo-page` capture a run against the sandbox and write `demo/live.html`, with the binding in `bindings/sandbox-petstore.binding.json`

build.description: `make generate` writes the collections and environments from the PIDL documents and `targets.json`
The signing helper's URL is an environment variable, `signer_url`, so a run can choose it
Docker Compose runs the sandbox with every role and the signing helper, on host ports set by `SIGNER_PORT` and `SANDBOX_HTTPS_PORT`, and the `test` profile runs the AAuth collection with Newman
The `petstore` profile runs the Petstore as an AAuth resource behind the sandbox, and its collection with Newman
The `omniagent` service chats with the Petstore as its agent
Sibling checkouts are located by org, in the `~/go/src/github.com/<org>/<repo>` layout, or set with `AAUTH_GO_DIR`, `PETSTORE_DIR` and `OMNIAGENT_DIR`

The make targets run pidl v0.10.0 with `go run` and fetch the AAuth document from the agent-protocols v0.9.0 release, so they need no checkouts; `PIDL`, `PIDL_VERSION`, `AAUTH_PROTOCOLS_VERSION`, `AAUTH_DOC` and `CURL` select other versions or local copies

documentation.description: README with the Docker quick start and the setup's two parts
Guide to running the collections against the sandbox: Docker or a local sandbox, how signing works, mock mode and regenerating
Interop testing runbook, for people and AI agents, for testing an agent, resource or server of your own against the sandbox
Documentation site at aistandards.io/aauth-postman, with the guides in `docs/guides/` and a new guide to the Petstore demos
